Start a background conversion; returns ``{jobId, status:"running"}``.

Accepts a rendered book (``.pdf``) or an authored one (``.md``); the conductor picks
the converter from the extension. If this exact file (by content hash) was already
ingested, returns ``{status:"duplicate", docId, ...}`` instead — pass ``?force=1`` to
re-ingest anyway.

The route keeps its ``/api/convert-pdf`` path: it is the documented seam the frontend
proxy and the status endpoint are both keyed to, and renaming it would break queued
clients for a cosmetic gain.

delete.description:
Delete a course outright: document row, every learn table keyed by it, its on-disk
artifacts, and its audiobooks. Irreversible.

The audiobooks are why this handler is not a pure pass-through. They live in
`supplemental/media` and `process/content` may not import it — the layering forbids a
sideways dependency — so `delete_document` takes a callback and the composition happens
here, at the one layer allowed to know about both (finding B5).

get.description:
What deleting a course would remove — source, versions, study rows, audiobooks —

Append one passive engagement event (read/listen/orient …).

The wire calls it ``scope`` and the column calls it ``section_key``; they are the same
value. This handler used to pass the whole body as one positional argument, which made
every call a TypeError — so no passive event was ever written and every read/listen
read-model has been rendering an empty set since it shipped.
